description:
Is your Instagram screentime begging for overtime pay? Are your friendships tested every time there is a Marvel vs DC debate?

If you are someone who knows the next brainrot song before it goes viral, join us to test your pop culture knowledge and stand a chance to win bragging rights and prizes!

The quiz will cover sitcoms, memes, entertainment, music, anime, and overall internet & pop culture. If you have never attended a quiz before, this is a great place to start. Every question is framed in a way that will let you work out the answer, and we are liberal with hints.

About Calm Your Wits:

Calm Your Wits Quizzing is a Bengaluru-based quizzing collective that curates and hosts engaging, beginner-friendly pub quizzes across India. Founded by quizmaster Sanket Mandal, they have expanded beyond the Bengaluru quizzing circuit to host regular events in Mumbai, Pune, Delhi, and Hyderabad. Launched with the intention of avoiding the intimidating archetype of traditional academic trivia, their style leans towards long-form questions, with lots of clues and audio-visual elements thrown in to help participants arrive at the answer. Quizmaster Sanket also draws heavily from humour on social media, cleverly using tweets, Instagram reels, and memes to make questions on even the most serious of topics. It’s a way of reminding people that all that doomscrolling can actually come in handy, and that knowledge can come from anywhere if we’re open to the possibilities. Expect questions that keep you guessing, hints that reward lateral thinking, and a few intentional misdirects that may have you arguing with your teammates. Come early, and come curious.

You can follow them on Instagram 
@calm.your.wits.quizzing

description:
Gossip! The Trivia Show Where Nothing Stays Secret.

You’ve always been the one who knew. Who told who. Who was seen where. Who said what and to whom and why it mattered.

Gossip is a live trivia game show built entirely around the world’s oldest currency — rumour, scandal, drama, and the stories people weren’t supposed to tell. Celebrity gossip, political scandals, historical intrigue, fictional drama, pop culture’s messiest moments, and the kind of story that starts with “okay don’t tell anyone but—”

Nothing is off the record. No reputation is safe. No secret stays buried.

If it was whispered, leaked, exposed, or absolutely none of your business — it’s fair game.

The Rumour Mill (Format & Rounds)

 Did You Hear? (Warm-up | ~20 mins)

Easy enough to get everyone talking. The kind of round where someone at your table will confidently say the wrong name and never live it down.

 The Grapevine (Main Rounds | ~60–75 mins)

Trivia, audio-visual rounds, identify-the-headline, and moments where you’ll either feel like the most informed person in the room or realise you’ve been completely out of the loop. Celebrity drama, political scandals, historical gossip, fictional rivalries, pop culture feuds, leaked moments, and everything in between.

 Face Off

Two tables. One piece of gossip. One team knows. The other thinks they do.

 The Bids

Bet your points. Someone will go all in on something they half-remember. That someone might be you.

 Surprise Round (whenever)

A twist nobody saw coming. That’s all we’re saying. Don’t spread it around.

How it works

Teams of up to 4 — come with your crew or we’ll find you one

Flying solo? We’ll sort you out

No gossip addiction required — just curiosity and a loose definition of “need to know”

Prizes for the winners, a good time for everyone else

You’ve always known more than you let on.

Gossip is where you prove it.

Who is Tasty Trivia?

Saloni and Susovan are the co-curators of Tasty Trivia — Ashoka University alums who turned a shared love for curiosity into a live, fun, silly trivia game show series. They design every show, question, and experience themselves, and have taken it across 6 cities with a monthly run in Bangalore. They are eyeing to take the show to the Edinburgh Fringe Festival in 2027.

description:
Got a ukulele or guitar gathering dust in the corner? Or just curious to pick up something new? This workshop is for you. We’ll dust off those instruments, warm up together, and by the end of the session, we’ll be jamming as a group, playing a song based on the theme together. Aanchal will break down the songs through a songwriter’s lens, sharing the history behind them too.

If you don’t have an instrument but just want to sing along? You’re welcome to join as well. We’ll be teaching a few vocal warmups and jamming the song together.

What to bring: An instrument, if you have one. A song sheet will be provided.

As a ukulele teacher, Kaviya’s been asked more than a few times if she knows a guitar teacher too, or if the same song can be played on guitar. That’s how this idea was born: what if we just brought our instruments we have, learned it and played together?

Why the theme “Freedom”?

What started as an idea to bring people together after what happened at Sansad Marg led us to explore songs of revolution and we finally settled on the word freedom, in any sense of it.

Bring your own idea of freedom to discuss with Aanchal, who brings a wealth of knowledge and shares her perspective and the history behind songs rooted in freedom, in all its forms.

And after months of trying to curate something together, we’re finally bringing this workshop to life.

Who is Aanchal Bordoloi?

I’m a 25 year old Assamese singer-songwriter based in Bangalore with the experience of performing in venues across the country. I have also been a member of The Vienna Songwriter Circle, Austria when I was 16 and have performed in venues there. The Indian Music Diaries Awards had selected me as one of the best debut artists in 2022. Rolling Stone Magazine had listed my debut single, Whiskey Blues as one of the best singles released in 2021, and my debut EP Letters To Bombay as one amongst the top 10 EPs released in 2024. Lianne La Havas, Laura Marling, Bob Dylan and Mumford and Sons are some of my musical influences.

Who is Kaviya S?

A music teacher, songwriter, an artist with over 3 years of teaching experience, performing across Bangalore and Coimbatore while guiding students online from all across India. Her writing explores womanhood, everyday mundane, change, time and societal issues she deeply cares about in her spoken poetry and songs. She’s inspired by poets and indie song writers like Megha Rao, Ditty, Frizzell and Lizzy McAlpine.

She’s also taught in a music school in Bangalore and conducted workshops in Indian Music Experience, Goa Ukulele Festival and many cafes in Bangalore and Coimbatore. She believes anyone can learn music and pick up the ukulele, whether you’re 5 or 50, or have never touched an instrument before. She’s driven by her love for writing songs to make sense of the world and all its epiphanies. When she’s not teaching, she’s reading poetry that moves her, taking long walks or spending hours with her friends.

A museum of our own.

Objects are heavy with meaning. What could look like an old toy may be dear to a person who had memories from childhood or maybe from their grandparents. As a kid, I collected pebbles just because they made me happy. My mom treasures a saree as a symbol of a certain time. My grandma repurposed an old headboard into a balcony railing because it once belonged to her mother, who napped on it every afternoon.

What are your favorite objects? A book you keep coming back to? A keepsake? A postcard? A creative experiment?

For this Slow Sunday, bring something meaningful and let’s create our own little museum. Things on display will inspire us to share stories, write, draw. Imagine this as a morning-long exhibition, created by you who attend and never to be experienced again.

This is an extra special Slow Sunday, as we celebrate the two-year anniversary of the Eleven AM Club. The club is shaped by each of you — no two gatherings are the same because it’s shaped by you who attend so we are kicking off the birthday month celebrating you and your stories.

Agenda

This will be a discussion focused session.

In a previous IWCB session, we talked about the journey of a blog post from idea to publication. In this session, we want to talk about the life of a blog post 
after
 you publish it.

Do you edit your blog posts after you’ve published them? What kinds of edits do you allow yourself to make? Would you ever consider deleting a piece of writing you’ve already published?

Do you share your blog posts with your friends? What about the communities you’re part of? What drives you to share your writing in this way?

What are your feelings about likes, shares, analytics, or other engagement metrics on your writing? Do you like to track such metrics?

Do you ever go back to read your old blog posts? Why or why not?

Have you ever thought about what you’d like your writing to add up to in the long term? In ten or fifteen years, are you hoping to tell a story, or meander through different ones?

We’ll spend the last hour of the meetup writing and publishing a piece on our personal websites. We’ll provide writing prompts to get you started.

Remember to bring a device you can use to write and post to your blog!

We are a Bangalore-based community-theatre troupe, working towards spreading the art of spontaneous storytelling & unscripted stagecraft, and rekindling the joy of being playful & whimsical. We meet on Wednesdays for Jams, and on weekends for workshops.
